A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same fine-tuning and Retention-Based Masking study. Their complete text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support comparison. Experimental details and proofs can be matched despite relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V2 reports original synthetic experiments in Figures 1–2, CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 evaluations in Tables 1–2, and feature visualizations in Figure 3.

after.justification: V3 retains these original results and adds TinyImageNet and SVHN evaluations in Appendix B.2, Tables 3–4.

M1.justification: The linear learning procedures, retention-based saliency mask, optimization objective, and parameter updates remain unchanged, including Equations (6)–(10). The ViT experiments apply the existing method without documenting a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: V3 adds TinyImageNet's 200-class image classification coverage and SVHN digit recognition to the existing CIFAR evaluations. These substantially broaden the represented image data and recognition domains; the original synthetic and CIFAR scenarios remain.

E2.justification: The CIFAR comparisons retain fine-tuning, SalUn, and retraining. The new TinyImageNet and SVHN tables reuse SalUn and retraining as comparators without introducing another comparison method.

E3.justification: Existing synthetic and CIFAR settings remain unchanged. The added evaluations introduce protocols with 10% random forgetting and 50% masking, including an SVHN configuration using ViT-Tiny and separately specified learning rates. These extend the evaluation settings without revising the retained experiments.

E4.justification: Appendix B.2 newly reports a SalUn learning-rate sweep from 6×10^-4 to 2×10^-3, identifying 1×10^-3 as best on SVHN, although individual sweep scores are absent. Existing feature-overlap analyses, fine-tuning sample-size experiments, and t-SNE visualizations are retained.

E5.justification: Table 2 retains mean and standard deviation reporting across five seeds. However, the added benchmark Tables 3–4 report only point estimates without run counts or uncertainty, making statistical reporting less complete across the benchmark comparisons. This does not establish a change in actual run counts.

E6.justification: The original tables and figures retain their results, while Tables 3–4 add outcomes for two substantially different evaluation settings. RBM versus SalUn average disparity is 4.39 versus 5.11 on TinyImageNet and 2.39 versus 2.57 on SVHN. SalUn nevertheless has higher retaining accuracy in both new comparisons.

T1.justification: The mathematical assumptions, optimization definitions, loss expressions, and proofs are retained. V2 Theorems 1–3 correspond to v3 Theorems 3.2, 3.4, and 4.1; Appendix B proofs become Appendix C. Differences concern numbering, reference labels, and typesetting.

C1.justification: The central fine-tuning analysis and RBM contribution claims remain. The conclusion modestly narrows its comparison claim from 'existing masking approaches' to 'forgotten-based masking approaches.' The revised novelty wording in the abstract otherwise preserves the original meaning.

C2.justification: New Appendix A explicitly acknowledges the limitations of linear regression, idealized feature assumptions, moderate-scale datasets, and fine-tuning baselines. Appendix B.2 adds interpretations of the new experiments, but its SVHN claim of superiority across all metrics conflicts with Table 4: RBM retaining accuracy is 94.12 versus SalUn's 95.93.

D1.justification: Appendix B.2 adds TinyImageNet sample counts, forgetting and masking fractions, ViT-Tiny's approximate 5.7M parameters, and learning-rate details. The existing CIFAR implementation paragraph moves from v2 Appendix A.2 to v3 Section 5.2 without changing its settings.

R1.justification: Section 1.1 adds citations and discussion of Torkzadehmahani et al.'s localized unlearning, Foster et al.'s selective synaptic dampening, and Chien et al.'s Langevin unlearning. These refine the contrast with retention-based masking and the positioning of the theoretical analysis.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence remain. V3 moves implementation details and the t-SNE discussion into Section 5.2, adds a Discussion appendix, and revises citation style, affiliations, and cross-references. Some assumptions and corollaries are now incorrectly referenced as theorems.

P2.justification: V3 comprehensively adopts journal typography, a reorganized author block, running headers, and denser page layout. It adds Tables 3–4 and moves Figure 3 from the appendix into the main text. All three original figures retain identical image content despite placement and sizing changes.

improvement.justification: V3 modestly strengthens applicability evidence beyond v2's CIFAR/ResNet-18 evaluations through TinyImageNet and SVHN/ViT-Tiny experiments, while explicitly acknowledging theoretical and empirical limitations. The benefit is limited by missing uncertainty for the new results and the unsupported claim of superiority across every SVHN metric. The original method and theoretical support remain unchanged.
